references.text: Job describes those who are 'enemies of the light' – those who rebel against the light and do not know its ways. They kill, steal, and commit adultery in the dark, and they dread the morning light. See [ref:Job 24:13-17|Job 24:13-17].

Proverbs describes the way of the wicked as darkness – they do not know what they are stumbling over. In contrast to the path of the righteous, which shines, the evil prefer darkness. See [ref:Prov 4:18-19|Proverbs 4:18-19].

Isaiah describes a rebellious people who will not listen to the Lord's law, saying to the seers 'you shall not see' and to the prophets 'do not prophesy truth to us.' They reject the light from God's word because it exposes their wickedness. See [ref:Isa 30:9-11|Isaiah 30:9-11].

The light shines in the darkness, but the darkness has not accepted it. Already in the prologue to the Gospel of John, the contrast between light and darkness is established, which is further developed in chapter 3. See [ref:John 1:5|John 1:5].

The preceding verse explains the judgment: the light has come into the world, but people loved darkness more than the light, because their deeds were evil. This provides the direct context for verse 20. See [ref:John 3:19|John 3:19].

In contrast to verse 20, this verse describes the one who does what is true and comes to the light, so that it may be made clear that his deeds have been done in God. Light and darkness are set as opposites. See [ref:John 3:21|John 3:21].

Jesus says that the world hates him because he testifies that its deeds are evil. This is a direct parallel: the one who does evil hates the light because it exposes their deeds. See [ref:John 7:7|John 7:7].

Jesus says that the world has seen his deeds and yet hates both him and the Father. They have no excuse for their sin, but they hate the light that was revealed through Jesus' words and deeds. See [ref:John 15:22-24|John 15:22-24].

Paul describes people who know God's righteous judgment, yet continue to do evil and even give their approval to others who do the same. They choose wickedness despite knowing the truth. See [ref:Rom 1:32|Romans 1:32].

Paul urges believers to put aside the deeds of darkness and put on the weapons of light. The expression 'deeds of darkness' directly connects to the idea that those who do evil prefer darkness. See [ref:Rom 13:12|Romans 13:12].

Paul exhorts believers not to have fellowship with the unfruitful deeds of darkness, but rather to expose them. The light exposes and rebukes what is hidden, which corresponds to the idea that the wicked avoid the light so their deeds will not be revealed. See [ref:Eph 5:11-13|Ephesians 5:11-13].
